description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates how the absolute mean (“Abs Mean”) of hidden states varies across network depth (“Layer”) for three conditions. The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” appears linear, and spans roughly from layer 1 to about layer 22, with numeric ticks shown at 5-layer intervals (5, 10, 15, 20). The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean,” appears linear, and ranges from about 0 up to slightly above 5, with labeled ticks at integer values (0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5). Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (no markers) labeled “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71,” which starts near ~0.2 at the first layer, increases gradually to around ~1.5 by roughly layer 12, continues upward to about ~2.0 by around layer 17, then rises more sharply after ~layer 18, reaching roughly ~2.5 near layer 19–20 and jumping to above ~4 and then above ~5 by the final layers; an orange dotted line (no markers) labeled “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05,” which increases approximately linearly from near ~0.1 at early layers to about ~2.0 by the last layer; and a green solid line (no markers) labeled “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04,” which similarly increases roughly linearly from near ~0.1 at the first layer to about ~2.0 at the final layer, closely tracking the orange line across the full layer range.
